anchors: is made only when you can answer that entry's `reopen_if` with what changed; without that answer, keep the decision
decision: Before the first edit of a skill, read its live rejected and removed decisions; reverse one only with an answer to its reopen_if.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-05: a per-skill decision ledger that the skill-writer reads

reopen_if: Editors meet the decisions some other way that is enforced (for example the edit guard alone), or the ledger is dropped.
why: Skills were changed forward and back because the reason for a change was not where the next editor looked; the history scan found two flips and two drop-then-restore cases.

anchors: first record its load-bearing rules as `rule` entries with `"origin": "baseline"`, in a commit of their own
decision: A skill with no rule entries gets its load-bearing rules recorded as baseline entries, in their own commit, before a rewrite or an A/B test.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-05: seed now, then baseline each skill on first touch

reopen_if: Rewrites keep dropping rules that no baseline entry recorded.
why: Backfilling every skill at once costs more than it saves; recording the baseline at the first rewrite gives the gate something to check the rewrite against.

anchors: `python3 plugins/bitranox/hooks/skill_decisions.py add --from-file <entries.json>`, never by editing the ledger
decision: Every decision an edit makes becomes a ledger entry, written only through skill_decisions.py add, once the new text exists.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-05: decisions recorded with their reasons, written through a CLI

reopen_if: The ledger format or its CLI changes.
why: A decision recorded only in a checklist or a commit body is not where the next editor looks, and a hand-edited ledger skips validation and the anchor check.

anchors: quote 20 to 200 characters that are the stable core of one rule
decision: An anchor is 20 to 200 characters of the stable core of one rule, unique in the skill, not a heading or table row.

evidence.text: anchor replay probe over the histories of three skills (plan M0, outcome A)

reopen_if: The refusal log shows rewordings outnumbering meaning changes over 30 days.
why: Anchors picked this way caught every real rule change in a replay of three skills' histories while re-wraps, table re-padding and list renumbering moved none.

anchors: on one line the commit gate reads: `Decisions: <id>, <id>`
decision: A SKILL.md change's checklist carries one Decisions line naming the entries it recorded, or none with a reason.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-05 approving the plan's rule D4

reopen_if: Most checklists say none, so the line adds ceremony without catching anything.
why: The commit gate can then check that a change states what it decided, without a ledger entry for changes that decide nothing.

decision: A narrative history file per skill.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-05: a decision ledger rather than a history file

reopen_if: An editor needs history that the ledger plus git log cannot answer.
why: git and CHANGELOG already hold the narrative, and a record rewritten wholesale loses items without a trace; a ledger keyed by decision with append-only entries does not.

anchors: The skill's decision ledger (Step 0b) holds decisions about the skill's TEXT only
decision: A decision about a bundled script or hook goes in a Decisions block in that file's module docstring, each decision naming the test that pins it; the skill's ledger holds decisions about the skill's text only.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-05 (code scope: hooks, jigs and scripts keep their reason in a module docstring Decisions block plus a regression test, no ledger file)

reopen_if: A reverted script or hook decision is found whose docstring block and tests both carried it and it was still undone.
why: Code keeps its reason where the next editor of the file reads it, beside a test that fails when the decision is reverted; a ledger entry cannot anchor on code, and a second record would drift from the docstring and the tests.

anchors: substitute the text's own definition literally and run that
decision: When the edited text defines a placeholder or path and builds a command on it, substitute the text's own definition literally and run that command before counting GREEN.

evidence.text: Queue entry 53 (M3 Task 3.4, 2026-11-06). GREEN opus and haiku refused to call GREEN done and ran the literal substitution.

reopen_if: Probes are given a way to execute the literal text themselves.
why: A step defined <plugin> as the checkout root, so its literal command named a missing script (rc 2), while three GREEN probes inferred the right path and passed.

anchors: a defect in it fakes a result
decision: Before dispatching a probe, check the outgoing prompt: no placeholder left, background sentences verified against the code, no scoring field the probe can read.

evidence.text: Each reported from a real probe run; not re-measured in this change.

reopen_if: A check made automatically at dispatch makes the prose redundant.
why: Each of the three defects fakes a result: a placeholder arm answers from nothing, a simplified background sentence manufactures a phantom gap, a readable answer turns the probe into an echo.

anchors: Run a headless `claude -p` subject with `--output-format stream-json --verbose`
decision: A headless claude -p probe subject runs with stream-json output and is read from the first assistant text block.

evidence.text: Scripted probe with a throwaway Stop hook on haiku: plain -p printed only the hook-reply text; stream-json held the real answer as the first assistant text block.

reopen_if: The CLI stops reporting the hook-driven continuation as the result text.
why: A Stop hook that blocks the end of the turn makes plain -p print the model's reply to the hook instead of its answer.

anchors: chains the gate's own refusal first
decision: An edit appending a check after a gate in a bash block chains the gate's refusal first and runs the block with the gate failing and passing.

evidence.text: bash -c 'false; test -z ""' exits 0; with the chained refusal it exits 1.

reopen_if: Skill bash blocks stop being copied as gates.
why: The block's exit code is otherwise the appended check's, so a red gate reads green.

anchors: Fix an overflow by reflowing the WHOLE paragraph
decision: Fix an overflow by reflowing the whole paragraph, and keep inline code spans whole.

evidence.text: mdwrap at width 50 split an inline code span on a scratch paragraph; the extended check reported a planted odd-backtick line.

reopen_if: The width check starts reflowing by itself.
why: One-line fixes push the overflow onto the next line, and a split span makes the skill unsearchable on the literal error string it quotes.

anchors: read the sentence that INTRODUCES the list
decision: When a bullet or row is added, the sentence introducing the list is read and its number word fixed.

evidence.text: Reported twice from fold work; not re-measured in this change.

reopen_if: A mechanical check catches stale list counts.
why: A quote-back passes on presence, so a list of four under a sentence promising three ships unseen.

anchors: A bold lead must stay true without its paragraph
decision: A bold lead must stay true without its paragraph; a tier-split quote-back points at the lead first.

evidence.text: Reported from a fold where haiku answered wrong until the lead was reworded; not re-measured in this change.

reopen_if: Tier-split quote-backs stop tracing to the lead.
why: A weak tier quotes the lead and misses the paragraph's detail, while a capable one quotes the detail.

anchors: deliberate rewording listed as an expected miss
decision: Splitting a SKILL.md moves text verbatim, proves no line was lost, repoints crossings, extends scanning tests and probes routing on both tiers.

evidence.text: Reported from one skill split; not re-measured in this change.

reopen_if: A tool performs the split and its checks.
why: The line check is the only proof no rule dropped; a SKILL.md-scanning test silently stops covering what moved; routing gaps show up only in a probe.
